title: Why your memories are NOT perfect recordings of the past
hook: Your memories are not always faithful to what actually happened.

narration.text: Your memories are not always faithful to what actually happened.
Over time, details can subtly shift or even be invented.
This is called reconstructive memory, and it is how our brains work.
When you recall an event, your brain reconstructs it from fragments.
It fills in gaps using general knowledge and current feelings.
This means each time you remember something, it can change slightly.
It explains why two people can remember the same event differently.
Have you ever realised a memory was not quite right?

description: Ever wondered why your memories sometimes feel a little off? It is not just you. This video explains reconstructive memory, showing how our brains actively rebuild past events, often changing details along the way. Discover why your memories are not perfect recordings.
topic: Why your memory sometimes changes details over time, explaining reconstructive memory.
